Spatial SVG benchmark — real-data results

Output folder: /tmp/claude-0/simtest3. Samples: sim7, sim7b. Methods run: kmeans_pca, gmm_pca, kmeans_smooth, ward_spatial, spectral_spatial. SplitStab replicates B = 4.

Example slice

1. Spatial domains (R1)

Across 2 slices, the pruned co-association ensemble (PCE) does not reliably differ from the majority vote of Kang et al. (mean ΔARI = +0.033, 95% bootstrap CI -0.023 to +0.089; better in 1/2 slices). Relative to the best single method on each slice (known only in hindsight), PCE differs by -0.048 ARI — the closer to zero, the more pruning recovers the oracle choice without labels.

2. Double dipping: slice-calibrated null (R2)

Counts are regenerated from each slice's own gene means, dispersions and library sizes, but with no spatial or domain structure. Every call here is a false positive. Same-data pipelines (domains and tests on the same counts) show how many spurious domain markers double dipping creates; the count-split rows and SplitStab should be near zero.

3. Semi-synthetic spike-in on real slices (R3)

Known markers are implanted into real low-autocorrelation genes inside one annotated layer. Recall is measured on the spiked genes; the false-call rate is measured on the remaining low-autocorrelation genes, which are presumed (not known) to be non-spatial.

4. Adjacent-section replication (R4)

Sections from the same donor 10 µm apart should share most true SVGs. Higher Jaccard and replication rate mean a more reproducible list (no ground truth needed). A list can replicate well by being short, so read this together with list sizes (n_a, n_b).

7. Uncertainty: does it mean something biologically?

Spots. A 55 µm Visium spot holds roughly 1–10 cells. At a layer boundary it holds cells from both layers, so its domain is genuinely ambiguous. If our per-spot uncertainty is biologically meaningful, confidence (agreement among kept methods) and replicate stability (how often the spot stays with the same neighbours when the tissue is resampled) should be lower at manually annotated boundaries (positive Spearman with distance to boundary) and confident spots should be more often correct.

How to read this report

  • PCE: label-free method scores (stability × agreement × spatial coherence) → pre-registered pruning → weighted co-association consensus with per-spot confidence.
  • SplitStab combined (proposed): domains on one half of each count (count splitting), markers tested on the other half among confident spots with a depth-aware NB test (liberal per-replicate rule: q < 0.1, rate ratio ≥ 1.2), a spatial gate (ACAT of Moran's I + SPARK-X-like on the held-out half), repeated B times with spot subsampling; synthetic NB negative-control genes calibrate the π threshold to an estimated FDP ≤ 0.1.
  • SplitStab strict (v2): the same with the strict per-replicate rule (q < 0.05, rate ratio ≥ 1.5). v1 stability: the pilot method (perturbed replicates, liberal SpaGCN rule, same counts, π ≥ 0.6), kept as an ablation.
  • Kang 2025 pipeline: one run per method → aligned majority vote → SpaGCN rule (q < 0.05, in-domain fraction ≥ 0.8, fold change ≥ 1.5) on the same counts.
  • Gene-level outputs: <sample>/domain_svgs.csv (selection probability π per gene) and global_svgs.csv.
